name: Reality Proxy
summary: In mixed reality, gazing at a real object and pinching lays out small proxies of the real objects around it next to the hand, and the user selects a distant, crowded or partly hidden object by touching its proxy instead of the object itself.
howItWorks: Built on Gaze + Pinch for physical objects on Apple Vision Pro. The user looks at a real object and pinches; the system detects the objects in the gaze region, slightly enlarged around the gaze point, and places a fixed-size proxy for each one near the hand, rescaled so their left/right and front/back layout matches the real scene. The proxies stay put after the pinch is released and lazily follow the hand. Touching a proxy with a fingertip selects its real object, which is highlighted in place; sliding the finger across proxies previews each object (skimming). AI adds semantic attributes and a spatial hierarchy to the proxies, so the same layout supports two-hand brushing to select several objects, selecting every object that shares an attribute, a two-hand zoom between a group and its parts (e.g. floors and rooms of a building), and user-made groups. Partly hidden objects can be reached through their proxies; fully hidden ones only when a digital twin or tracking data provides their positions. Evaluated in an expert review with 10 XR specialists (office information retrieval and building navigation tasks), with no baseline comparison.
advantages: Distant, crowded or partly occluded real objects become easy to reach, without stretching the arm or precise aiming.
The same proxies support multi-object selection, attribute-based filtering and moving through a spatial hierarchy with familiar gestures.
limitations: Objects that are fully hidden are not detected by the vision pipeline unless a digital twin or tracking data is available.
Touching a proxy can trigger unintended selections while the user is attending to the physical world.
Mapping proxies back to real objects adds cognitive load; only an expert review, with no baseline comparison.

relationships.note: Keeps Gaze + Pinch to start a selection and moves it to physical objects in MR; proxies appear on the same pinch.
Selects through a stand-in near the hand, but with fixed-size abstract proxies rather than a scaled copy of the scene.
Discussed as an alternative way of reaching objects beyond arm's reach.
